en.question: Users report that a Claude-powered feature "sometimes returns nonsense". What is the most effective first diagnostic step?

options.text: Capture full traces of failing cases and look for a common pattern.
Move the feature to a larger model and see whether the reports subside.
options.note: Changing a variable before understanding the failure is expensive guessing.

options.text: Rewrite the prompt from scratch using the current best-practice guidance.
options.note: A blind rewrite may fix it, break something else, or do nothing, unmeasurably.

options.text: Add a disclaimer to the interface warning that output may be inaccurate.
options.note: A disclaimer manages expectations without addressing the defect.

en.explanation: You cannot fix an intermittent failure you cannot reproduce. Complete traces reveal whether the cause is truncation, a particular input shape, a parameter difference, or a tool returning bad data.
